text:
morgan: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing a compact telemetry header for inference requests so we can attach model / batch metadata upstream without exploding metric/trace cardinality.

morgan: Idea: one header (X-RI-Tel) carrying a tiny binary envelope (proto v0) with fields: model_id, model_variant, quant_profile, batch_hint, request_tier. Base64 in HTTP.

alisha: sounds useful. main worry is backwards compatibility with older proxies and log shipping agents. how do we fail-open? :thinking:

devin: fail-open plan: header optional. if absent, fallback to current parsing of logs/traces. ingress proxies should forward header verbatim. we should add a shim at edge to synthesize when we can (e.g., from route + model header).

sanjay: curious about cardinality: model_id and model_variant are high-card fields if teams create ad-hoc variants. do we normalize or apply a small-name registry?

morgan: yes — registry is key. registry maps (human name -> stable canonical id). registry enforced on model onboarding; unsupported values get collapsed to "custom" bucket in ingest.

tia: what about sampling? if trace sampler drops spans, can we keep header-derived counters in metrics pipeline so cost attribution remains accurate?

devin: we should emit a lightweight counter event at ingress with the canonical id and token counts; those counters go to cost-agg pipeline and are independent of trace sampling. header enables cheap, low-cardinality metrics (model_id, seq_len_bucket, tokens).

kevin: implementation nit: proto v0 layout (pseudocode):
```
message TelV0 {
  string model_id = 1;
  string variant = 2;
  uint32 quant_profile = 3;
  uint32 batch_hint = 4;
  uint32 tokens = 5;
}
```
encoded -> base64. ingress agents decode for local metrics and forward raw header to ingest.

alisha: can we reserve a tiny JSON fallback for environments that strip binary headers? e.g., X-RI-Tel-JSON with same fields but only for dev mode.

morgan: agreed — JSON fallback but documented as higher-cardinality and rate-limited. prefer binary for production.

sanjay: security: header might contain sensitive onboarding tags. ensure we only include stable ids, no customer PII. add automated check in SDKs to block any free-form metadata.

devin: ops-bot: deploy-check for telemetry header shim?

ops-bot: deploy-check queued — blocked: need ingress proxy change and SDK bump. ETA: 2w for canary if specs + tests are in a PR.

morgan: next steps: 1) write spec (proto + registry contract) 2) implement shim in ingress proxy (forward + local counter emit) 3) add registry enforcement to model onboarding 4) instrument cost-agg to accept header counters. volunteers?

kevin: I can own proto + ingress shim.

alisha: I'll scope SDK changes and fallback JSON.

devin: I'll do cost-agg plumbing and counter schema.

morgan: thanks — I'll draft the spec and post the RFC update. small follow-up: please think about how this interacts with prefix/KV caching telemetry (we want per-model cache hit attribution).

sanjay: noted. relating cache hits to header canonical id should be straightforward if caches log the canonical id on hit.

morgan: cool. :thumbsup:

tia: quick ask: include one integration test that shows attribution with sampled traces vs counters so we can validate reconciliation.

morgan: yep will add.

kevin: +1

ops-bot: reminder: please add a privacy review ticket for the header registry before canary.
